```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(ggplot2)
library(ggsubplot)
```

A subplot layer places a small ggplot2 layer at each major location. The major
mapping locates the boxes; the minor mapping describes their contents. These
layers work with ordinary ggplot2 plots, themes, scales, coordinates, and
`ggsave()`.

The bundled `nasa` and `casualties` objects are entirely synthetic. Their names
and columns preserve historical example compatibility; they contain no real
NASA observations or Afghan War Diary records. All plots below using these
objects illustrate fictional data.

Use `group` to identify the observations belonging to each box. Major x and y
must be constant within each group; expressions such as `mean(long)` and
`mean(lat)` can locate groups with varying coordinates.

```{r nasa-points}
n <- subset(nasa, year == 1995 & long > -100 & long < -90 & lat > 30 & lat < 40)
ggplot(n) +
  geom_subplot(aes(long, lat, group = id),
    subplot = geom_point(aes(month, surftemp)),
    width = 2, height = 2, reference = ref_box()) +
  coord_quickmap() + labs(x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude")
```

`width` and `height` are measured in major coordinate units. The default
`rel(0.95)` uses 95% of the smallest distance between distinct centres along
that axis, or 95% of one unit when there is only one centre. Minor x and y
positions, including bar edges and line endpoints, are scaled together into
the boxes. Minor limits are shared by default. Set `x_scale = free` or
`y_scale = free` to use separate limits for each box; this highlights shapes
but removes direct magnitude comparisons along that axis.

For compatibility, the minor layer can still be captured inside `aes()`:

```{r historical-spelling}
ggplot(n) + geom_subplot(aes(long, lat, group = id,
  subplot = geom_line(aes(month, surftemp))), width = 2, height = 2) +
  coord_quickmap()
```

Minor aesthetics are evaluated within each subplot. For example,
`fill = mean(surftemp)` gives one colour to every row in a location. Use
`ply.aes = FALSE` to evaluate minor expressions on the entire layer data, or
`ply.aes = c("fill")` to evaluate only fill within each subplot. `I()` has its
normal ggplot2 meaning: an identity aesthetic, such as `colour = I("red")`.
Expressions containing `after_stat()`, `after_scale()`, or `stage()` are
handled by ggplot2. Legends and explicit non-position scales are shared with
the outer plot.

```{r stars}
ggplot(n) + geom_subplot(aes(long, lat, group = id),
  subplot = geom_star(aes(angle = month,
    r = (surftemp - min(surftemp)) / (max(surftemp) - min(surftemp)),
    fill = mean(surftemp))), width = 2, height = 2) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Mean temperature (K)") + coord_quickmap()
```

`geom_subplot2d()` assigns rows to a grid using `cut(..., include.lowest = TRUE)`.
Supply `bins`, `binwidth`, or explicit x/y `breaks` (in decreasing precedence:
breaks, binwidth, bins). Missing and out-of-range locations are omitted. Grid
centres are cell midpoints, and unequal break spacing gives unequal box sizes.
Only occupied cells are drawn. Reference boxes are supplied by default.

```{r casualties}
c <- subset(casualties, year == 2004 & lon > 60 & lon < 75 & lat > 29 & lat < 39)
p <- ggplot(c) + geom_subplot2d(aes(lon, lat), bins = c(5, 4),
  subplot = geom_bar(aes(victim, fill = victim)), y_scale = free) +
  coord_quickmap() + labs(x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude")
if (requireNamespace("maps", quietly = TRUE)) {
  afghanistan <- map_data("world", region = "Afghanistan")
  p <- ggplot(c) + geom_polygon(data = afghanistan,
    aes(long, lat, group = group), fill = "grey97", colour = "grey60") +
    p$layers + coord_quickmap() + labs(x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude")
}
p
```

Coxcombs use sector **areas** for counts, so radii are proportional to the
square root of counts. Different fill groups in a sector stack in area.
The default stat counts categorical angles; numeric histograms use
`stat = "bin"` with explicit `bins` or `binwidth`. Frequency stars use the
same counting choices. Ordinary stars take `angle` and `r` directly.

```{r coxcombs}
ggplot(c) + geom_subplot2d(aes(lon, lat), bins = c(5, 4),
  subplot = geom_coxcomb(aes(angle = month, fill = victim)),
  reference = NULL) + coord_quickmap()
```

`ref_box()`, `ref_hline()`, and `ref_vline()` create reference factories. Their
minor coordinates are already in `[-1, 1]` and are placed without further
normalization. Reference mappings are evaluated on the rows of each subplot,
then drawn once per occupied subplot.

Use `position = "merge"` to pool overlapping locations, including transitive
overlaps. The merged location is the mean of constituent centres; its box size
is the maximum original size on each axis. This adjustment aggregates data
before computing the minor stat.

```{r merging}
d <- data.frame(X = rep(c(0, .8, 1.6, 5), each = 3),
  id = rep(1:4, each = 3), a = rep(1:3, 4), b = 1:12)
ggplot(d) + geom_subplot(aes(X, 0, group = id),
  subplot = geom_point(aes(a, b)), width = 1, height = 1,
  position = "merge", reference = ref_box()) + coord_equal()
```

`ply_aes()` applies the grouped evaluator to an ordinary layer. It uses the
group aesthetic, or an explicit vector of column names in `.vars`.

```{r ply}
ggplot(mtcars) + ply_aes(geom_point(aes(wt, mpg, group = cyl,
  colour = mean(mpg)))) + labs(colour = "Mean mpg by cylinders")
```

Outer facets and nested subplots are unsupported and produce clear errors.
Major discrete coordinates become numeric positions; label their continuous
outer axes explicitly if needed. Minor layers take the rows assigned by the
subplot layer; put any layer-specific data on `geom_subplot()` itself.
